A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RLKV and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering, relocation, and revised displays, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark accuracies, inference measurements, training ablations, head-sensitivity experiments, and error analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds LongReason evaluation, continuous-batching measurements, and an inference-window ablation.

M1.justification: The mixed-attention gates, GRPO/L1 objective, training stabilization, and top-k head selection remain unchanged. Section 4.3 adds a serving adaptation previously described as future work: SGLang uses separate paged and circular-buffer KV pools, with freed memory reassigned to support more concurrent requests.

E1.justification: v3 adds LongReason with 64K inputs and a 70K context, substantially extending evaluation to a long-input scenario beyond the existing reasoning and knowledge benchmarks. It evaluates Llama-3.1-8B-R1 and Qwen-3-4B-Thinking there; the original training data, benchmark coverage, and motivation studies remain.

E2.justification: KVZip is added as a comparator throughout Figure 5 and the three complete benchmark tables, and participates in the new LongReason comparison. H2O, R-KV, and DuoAttention remain in the corresponding original benchmark sweeps, making this a focused expansion of the comparator set.

E3.justification: The fixed-batch Transformers/FlashAttention-2 efficiency experiment in v2 Table 2 is replaced by SGLang continuous batching on one A100 40GB, with varying concurrency and sparsity, in v3 Table 3. New protocols include 400 of 794 LongReason samples at 70K context and three sink/local-window configurations. These are substantial evaluation changes, not directly comparable reruns of the old efficiency setting.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused window-sensitivity ablation comparing 16+64, 32+128, and 64+256 tokens across sparsities, and explicitly examines transfer from 8K training rollouts to 70K evaluation. Existing training ablations, head-sensitivity tests, error analyses, and fixed-versus-dynamic-budget studies remain. The standalone single-layer latency/throughput analysis in v2 Figure 6 is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly acknowledges SGLang nondeterminism and resulting run-to-run accuracy variation for both RLKV and full attention. This is a qualitative uncertainty disclosure; no run counts, seeds, quantified variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All existing result rows in v2 Tables 4–6 are retained exactly in v3 Tables 6–8, alongside new KVZip rows. v3 adds LongReason, window-ablation, serving, and SGLang knowledge-summary results, while revising Table 1's selected operating points and omitting some older threshold-specific entries. Reported speedups change from 1.09–1.21× to 1.19–2.06× under different serving conditions, so this is replacement evidence rather than a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 introduces a compressed-pool memory estimate, O(max_running_requests × W), and the theoretical speedup limit 1/((1−s)+sW/L), based on residual cache costs. The original method definitions and Equations 1–4 remain substantively unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the headline claims from 20–50% to 20–60% near-lossless cache reduction and from at most 1.21× to 2.06× end-to-end speedup, specifying continuous batching at 60% reduction. These materially expand the claimed efficiency benefits, while the central RL-as-probe and reasoning-critical-head contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations about long-context transfer, window size extending the near-lossless range, and concurrency explaining practical speedups. Appendix G expands the former future-work discussion into explicit limitations concerning static gating, dynamic-decision overhead, and degradation at sparsity ≥0.8. Appendix B also identifies unsupported SGLang caching features, substantially clarifying applicability and deployment boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 documents SGLang v0.5.2, its dual-pool implementation and caching restrictions, serving hardware, and the different engines used for Table 1's math/code and knowledge results. Figure 3 revises the reported Qwen-2.5 KV group size from 8 to 7 and removes detailed head/layer counts, without establishing a model replacement. Training hyperparameters, training costs, prompt instructions, and project access information remain.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly credits prior head-reallocation methods for gated mixed attention and adds KVZip and LongReason references. Appendix G substantially broadens positioning toward an on-policy approach applicable to pruning, sparse attention, token compression, multimodal tasks, and agentic reasoning, with numerous newly cited works. Publication-year and venue updates elsewhere are bibliographic edits rather than new research relationships.

P1.justification: The revision tightens the method definition and qualitative-analysis prose, clarifies inference-time discretization, rewrites the conclusion, and moves expanded future-work material into Appendix G. It also adds acknowledgments and replaces the preprint notice with conference information. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes from three baseline-comparison blocks into a compact RLKV-only benchmark-by-model summary with knowledge rows. The old efficiency figure and table are replaced by new serving, LongReason, and window-ablation displays. Figure 5 gains KVZip curves, Figure 7's horizontal-axis label is clarified, and retained appendix figures and expanded numerical tables are substantially rearranged.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens practical-efficiency and generalization evidence through continuous-batching measurements, 70K-context evaluation, KVZip comparisons, and window sensitivity, while preserving the original benchmark results and documenting deployment limitations. Important qualifications remain: Table 3's 2.06× speedup accompanies 73.8% accuracy versus 79.4% for full attention, and Table 2 shows KVZip beating RLKV on Qwen-3 at sparsity 0.2 despite the broad superiority statement. These qualifications limit the strongest claims but do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
